guideTitle: 6 Best Soaker Hose Kits With Timers in 2026
metaTitle: 6 Best Soaker Hose Kits With Timers (2026)
metaDescription: Six soaker hose and timer options compared: a bundled 2-zone timer kit, two programmable faucet timers, and linkable hoses to pair them with.
introParagraphs: A soaker hose without a timer is a hose you will forget about, and a forgotten soaker either floods a bed or leaves it dry on the one day it mattered. Soaker hoses release water slowly, often over 30 to 90 minutes, so they are one of the few garden tools that really benefit from automation. The tricky part is that most listings sell either the hose or the timer, not both.

This guide separates the lineup honestly. Only the MIXC listing bundles a hose and a timer in one purchase. The two RAINPOINT models are programmable faucet timers built to drive a soaker hose, and the Secbulk, LINCHOC HOME and MQJIAZHI picks are hoses or hose systems that pair with any standard timer. We evaluated each on stated specs and buyer feedback, not on our own flow or battery measurements.

If you want one box with everything, start with the MIXC. If you already own a hose, the timers below show what scheduling features actually matter, from rain delay to brass threads that survive a pressure spike.

products.name: MIXC Thickened Soaker Hose 100 FT With 2-Zone Timer
products.description:
The MIXC is the only pick that puts a hose and a timer in one purchase. The timer is the ZL02 model, a rechargeable 2-zone unit with a built-in 3.7V 2000mAh lithium battery and a Type-C charging port, so there are no AA batteries to replace. The hose is a 100 foot thickened version with a 1 millimeter wall, double the 0.5 millimeters the maker cites for ordinary soaker hoses.

The connectors use copper joints locked by aluminum rings, and a long swivel handle makes twisting easier on the hands. Two zones means you can run two separate lines on different schedules, for example vegetables daily and shrubs twice a week. The maker is candid about limits: it suggests connecting no more than 50 feet at once and keeping pressure between 40 and 60 PSI, with the included washers installed.

In practice, the rechargeable battery is the standout, because no one wants to open a waterlogged battery cover in January. The tradeoff is that you charge it yourself, and you should check the charge level at the start of the season. Compared with the single-zone RAINPOINT timers, the MIXC gives two independent outlets and a rechargeable cell, but you commit to the maker's hose rather than choosing your own.

products.name: RAINPOINT Programmable Hose Timer With Brass Inlet and Outlet
products.description:
The upgraded RAINPOINT timer uses pure brass for both the water inlet and outlet threads, and the maker says it withstands up to 116 PSI. Built-in metal filter gaskets catch sediment before it reaches the hose. You program a start time, a watering duration from 1 minute to 3 hours 59 minutes, and a frequency from every 1 to 12 hours or every 1 to 7 days.

Rain delay mode pauses the schedule for 24, 48 or 72 hours and then resumes it automatically, and a manual mode runs the water for anywhere from 1 minute to 8 hours without disturbing the schedule. A big LCD shows duration, frequency and battery level, which helps if the screen is read from a standing position. This is a single-outlet timer, so it drives one hose, unlike the MIXC's two zones.

It is a standalone device that screws onto a spigot and then onto your hose. That gives freedom to pair it with any soaker, including the Secbulk or LINCHOC HOME hoses in this guide. Compared with the standard RAINPOINT model below, the brass threads and filter gaskets are the upgrade, and they matter most if your faucet pressure runs high.
products.bestFor: Buyers with strong spigot pressure who want brass threads, a filter and a flexible schedule.
pros: Brass inlet and outlet, rated to 116 PSI
Metal filter gaskets catch sediment
Rain delay and manual modes
Wide duration range up to 3 h 59 min
cons: Single outlet drives only one hose

products.name: RAINPOINT Programmable Garden Hose Timer, Single Outlet
products.description:
The standard RAINPOINT is the plain version of the same timer: a single-outlet, battery-powered unit with automatic, manual and rain delay modes. You set a start time, a duration from 1 minute to 3 hours 59 minutes, and a frequency from every hour to every 7 days. Manual mode lets you water on demand from 1 minute up to 8 hours without erasing the schedule.

A large LCD displays the schedule and battery status, and the unit runs on two AA alkaline batteries, which are not included. The listing says nothing about brass threads or a filter, so this version is the lighter-duty choice. It also has only one outlet, which limits you to a single zone compared with the MIXC's two zones.

Setup is straightforward: attach it to the faucet, connect the hose, program the schedule and press start. The rain delay is a real convenience for soaker hoses, because a long soak right after a storm wastes water. Choose this one if you want the least expensive way to automate a single line, and choose the brass RAINPOINT if your spigot pressure is on the high side.
products.bestFor: Gardeners automating a single soaker hose line on a typical household spigot.
pros: Automatic, manual and rain delay modes
Wide programming range
Large LCD is easy to read
Works with any soaker hose

products.name: Secbulk Flat Soaker Hose 100 FT (2 x 50 FT) With Stakes
specs: Bury under up to 3 inches of mulch

specList.label: Burial
specList.value: Up to 3 inches of mulch or soil

products.description:
The Secbulk is a pair of 50 foot flat soaker hoses with a PVC core and a clog-resistant fabric cover, plus stakes to hold them in place. The maker says it can be laid above ground or buried beneath up to 3 inches of mulch or soil, and the rust-resistant end caps allow linking or capping off. It states a best pressure of 40 to 90 PSI and warns that hot water is not suitable.

A flat hose is the right partner for a timer because it lies close to the soil and does not kink when the timer cycles on and off. The 40 to 90 PSI range is wider than the 40 to 60 PSI on the MIXC, which suggests more tolerance for a strong spigot but still calls for a regulator if you are above that. There is a one-year warranty on the hoses.

Because the listing is for hoses only, you will add a timer such as either RAINPOINT model. Compared with the LINCHOC HOME, it is lighter and flat rather than round, and it trades brass fittings for rust-resistant end caps. Pick it when you want to move the hose between beds each season and let a timer handle the schedule.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want a lightweight flat hose to pair with a faucet timer and rearrange each season.
pros: Two 50 ft sections link or run separately
Stakes included
Wide 40 to 90 PSI working range
Can sit under up to 3 inches of mulch

products.name: LINCHOC HOME 1/2 Inch Soaker Hose Kit With Brass Fittings
products.description:
The LINCHOC HOME is a 1/2 inch round soaker hose with solid brass connectors, sold in 10, 15, 25 and 50 foot individual hoses and in 100 and 150 foot kits with sturdy metal garden stakes. The maker describes the material as soft, stretchable and high in tensile strength, so it lays flat and bends easily. It is UV resistant and meant to resist kinking and daily wear.

Brass connectors are the longest-lasting fitting type among the hoses in this guide, and a timer that cycles daily puts repeated stress on the threads. The size range is also useful, because you can buy a short hose for a small bed or the 150 foot kit for a large plot. The tradeoff is that a 150 foot run is too long for even watering, so cut it into zones.

This listing is for the hose and stakes, with no timer included, so pair it with one of the RAINPOINT models. Compared with the Secbulk's flat fabric hoses, the LINCHOC is rounder and heavier, and better suited to a permanent layout. Compared with the MIXC bundle, it lets you choose your own timer, which is a plus if you already own one.
products.bestFor: Gardeners who want brass connectors and a choice of lengths to pair with their own timer.
pros: Solid brass connectors resist rust and cracking
Sizes from 10 ft to a 150 ft kit
Metal stakes included in the kits
Soft material bends without kinking
cons: 150 ft runs lose pressure at the end
Round hose is heavier than flat hoses

products.name: MQJIAZHI 230 FT 1/4 Inch Soaker Drip Irrigation Kit
products.description:
The MQJIAZHI 230 foot kit is a micro-drip system built around 197 feet of 1/4 inch soaker tubing and 33 feet of 5/16 inch main line. It ships with a Y-connector, connectors, an end cap, six reducing tees, six six-way connectors, 30 end plugs, thread seal tape and 20 ground stakes. The maker describes micro-pore seepage that waters along the whole line and says it resists clogging better than emitters.

The listing does not include a timer, so this is a system that expects you to add one at the faucet, which makes it a natural partner for either RAINPOINT model. The thin tubing is flexible enough for raised beds, borders, greenhouses and pots, and it can sit on the surface, under mulch or buried. The setup effort is the main cost, because you plan tees and connectors before anything waters.

Compared with the MIXC bundle, this kit covers far more ground and branches into many zones, but it needs a separate timer and more planning. Compared with the Secbulk or LINCHOC, it is a different philosophy: instead of one long hose, you build a network of short seeping lines.
products.bestFor: Large or complex gardens that need a branching soaker network driven by a faucet timer.
pros: Complete branching system with tees and connectors
197 ft of soaker tubing covers many beds
20 ground stakes included
Thin tubing bends around tight beds
cons: Thin tubing is easier to puncture

buyingCriteria.explanation: A bundle is simpler, but a separate timer gives you freedom to upgrade. Only the MIXC pairs a hose and a timer, and it ties you to the maker's hose. The RAINPOINT timers work with the Secbulk, LINCHOC HOME or MQJIAZHI systems and with any hose you already own. If you start with a bundle and the timer fails, you may need to buy a replacement regardless.

A zone is an independent watering line with its own schedule. The MIXC timer has 2 zones, while both RAINPOINT models have a single outlet. If you want vegetables watered daily and shrubs twice a week, two zones saves a second timer. You can also add a Y-splitter to a one-zone timer, but then both lines run on the same schedule.

Battery management is the least glamorous part of a timer, and it is where many fail. The MIXC has a built-in 2000mAh lithium battery with Type-C charging, while the RAINPOINT models take two AA alkaline batteries that are not included. Check the battery indicator at the start of each season, and bring a rechargeable unit indoors for winter if the maker advises it. A dead battery means a missed watering.

Soaker hoses need long, infrequent cycles, so look at the maximum duration. The RAINPOINT timers run from 1 minute to 3 hours 59 minutes with frequency from every hour to every 7 days. That covers most soakers at 30 to 90 minutes. Rain delay of 24, 48 or 72 hours is useful, because it pauses the schedule after a storm and resumes automatically.

Timers sit at the faucet where pressure is highest, so thread material matters. The upgraded RAINPOINT has pure brass inlet and outlet and withstands up to 116 PSI, with metal filter gaskets. Soaker hoses prefer lower pressure, so add a regulator even when the timer is robust. The MIXC suggests 40 to 60 PSI and the Secbulk lists 40 to 90 PSI as its best range.

Timers do not fix a hose that is too long, and long soakers water the front more than the back. The MIXC maker suggests no more than 50 feet connected at once, and the Secbulk comes as two 50 foot pieces for that reason. Brass connectors, as on the LINCHOC HOME, stand up to daily cycling better than plastic. Keep each zone under about 100 feet where possible.

howWeEvaluated.title: What is actually in the box
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked each listing for what ships together. The MIXC bundles a hose and a 2-zone timer, the RAINPOINT models are timers only, and the Secbulk, LINCHOC HOME and MQJIAZHI are hoses or systems without a timer. We labeled each pick accordingly rather than implying a kit that is not there.

howWeEvaluated.title: Scheduling features
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared duration, frequency, rain delay and manual modes. Both RAINPOINT timers share a 1 minute to 3 hour 59 minute duration and 24, 48 or 72 hour rain delay. The MIXC adds a second zone, which none of the other timers match.

howWeEvaluated.title: Pressure and thread durability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at stated pressure ranges and thread material. The brass RAINPOINT is rated to 116 PSI, the Secbulk lists 40 to 90 PSI as best, and the MIXC suggests 40 to 60 PSI. Brass connectors on the LINCHOC HOME scored well for daily cycling.

howWeEvaluated.title: Power and upkeep
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed battery type and care. The MIXC uses a rechargeable lithium cell with Type-C charging, while the RAINPOINT timers use two AA batteries that are not included. Hoses were compared on warranty and fittings, with the Secbulk at one year.

howWeEvaluated.title: Lineup positioning
howWeEvaluated.description: The MIXC leads the bundle and rechargeable power, the brass RAINPOINT leads pressure tolerance, the standard RAINPOINT leads simple automation, the Secbulk leads flat linkable hoses, the LINCHOC HOME leads brass fittings and length choices, and the MQJIAZHI leads branching coverage. These reads come from specs and buyer feedback, not our own run-time tests.

faq.q: Which soaker hose kit with a timer is best?
faq.a: The MIXC is the only listing that bundles a hose and a timer, with a rechargeable 2-zone controller. If you prefer to mix and match, pair the brass RAINPOINT timer with a Secbulk or LINCHOC HOME hose. Both routes give automatic watering.

faq.q: How long should I set the timer for a soaker hose?
faq.a: Many gardens need 30 to 90 minutes, depending on soil type. Sandy soil needs shorter, more frequent runs, while clay needs longer, less frequent ones. The RAINPOINT timers allow up to 3 hours 59 minutes.

faq.q: Do I need a rain delay feature?
faq.a: It is worth having. Rain delay pauses the schedule for 24, 48 or 72 hours on the RAINPOINT timers, then resumes automatically. That prevents a long soak right after a storm.

faq.q: Will a timer work with any soaker hose?
faq.a: Yes, a faucet timer screws onto a standard 3/4 inch spigot and then onto the hose. It should not be used with hot water, a warning the Secbulk makes explicit. Check the timer's pressure rating against your spigot.

faq.q: Why does my soaker hose only water the first part?
faq.a: Long runs lose pressure toward the end, so the far section gets less. The MIXC maker suggests no more than 50 feet connected at once. Use shorter zones or a regulator.

faq.q: How do I protect a timer in winter?
faq.a: Remove it before freezing weather, drain it and store it indoors. For the rechargeable MIXC, charge it before storing and recharge before spring. Battery-powered units should have the batteries removed.

faq.q: Should I choose a flat or round hose with a timer?
faq.a: Flat hoses like the Secbulk are lighter and easier to move, while round hoses like the LINCHOC HOME tend to last in permanent layouts. Either works with a timer. Pick based on how often you rearrange your beds.
